newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ National MP pleased with tax cut discussion.
newsitem.headline: NZ National MP pleased with tax cut discussion.

text.p: Maverick National Party MP John Bank said on Monday the party was making good progress in its discussion of tax cuts in the context of a proposed coalition deal with New Zealand First.
Banks, who adamantly opposes scrapping a planned second round of tax cuts next July, told reporters: "I can report that we are making good progress."
Banks said it would be wrong to detail what sort of progress had been made, but hinted there could be flexibility in the timing of further tax cuts.

"It may mean that the tax cuts are deferred, or it may mean that we spend X amount of money in health, social welfare and education, then deliver the tax promises at a later date. I would be much more comfortable with that," he said.
Asked if National had now worked out an agreement on tax cuts to take to New Zealand First, he said: "That's my understanding."
Banks said he was not alone among party MPs in his position on the tax cuts.
"I'm sure there's a lot of concern about this promise...This was a solemn promise on the basis that not only did we say we were going to do it, but we put it into law."
Asked if National would still deliver on the tax cuts, he said: "Please talk to the prime minister."
